title: Yakitori Chicken Skewers
subtitle: Japanese grilled chicken skewers with tare glaze
excerpt: Yakitori are Japanese grilled chicken skewers coated in a sticky soy and mirin glaze called tare. They are quick to make and equally good under a grill or on a barbecue. Threading the chicken alternately with spring onion is traditional and adds a gentle sweetness.
sourceNotes: Yakitori is a style of Japanese grilling that became widespread in the Meiji era as chicken became more available. Dedicated yakitori bars called yakitoriya are a fixture of Japanese city life.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales easily. Prepare all the skewers ahead and glaze just before cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the skewers up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate until ready to cook.

content.text: Soak wooden skewers in cold water for at least 30 minutes before use so they don't scorch under the grill. Thread the chicken and spring onion pieces alternately, leaving a little space at each end to handle.
Combine the soy, mirin, honey, sake, garlic and ginger in a small saucepan. Bring to the boil and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly syrupy. Leave to cool.
Thread the chicken and spring onion pieces alternately onto soaked wooden skewers. Place on a foil-lined baking tray.
Heat the grill to its highest setting. Brush the skewers generously with the tare glaze.
Grill for 5 to 6 minutes. Flip, brush again with glaze and grill for another 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through and lightly charred.
Brush with a final coat of tare and serve immediately with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Glaze burning before chicken is cooked
items.cause: Grill too close or too hot.
items.fix: Move the tray lower and grill more slowly.

items.cause: Breast meat used instead of thigh.
items.fix: Thigh is much more forgiving; switch for next time.
